sanskrit: naiva bhāgo 'tra bhīṣmasya droṇasya ca mahātmanaḥ tābhyām atītya tau bhāgau nihatā mama śatravaḥ
english: No share of this remained for Bhīṣma or for great-souled Droṇa; surpassing the share allotted to each, those two slew my enemies.

sanskrit: vṛddhau hi tau naravyāghrau chalena nihatau ca tau kṛtvā nasukaraṃ karma gatau svargam ito 'nagha
english: For those two tigers among men were aged, and they were brought down by guile; yet having wrought deeds hard to perform, they passed from here to heaven, O sinless one.

sanskrit: tathānye puruṣavyāghrāḥ parair vinihatā yudhi asmadīyāś ca bahavaḥ svargāyopagatā raṇe tyaktvā prāṇān yathāśakti ceṣṭāḥ kṛtvā ca puṣkalāḥ
english: So too other tigers among men were struck down in battle by the foe, and many of our own went forth to heaven in the fight, yielding up their lives and performing, to the utmost of their strength, deeds rich and abundant.

sanskrit: karṇo hy eko mahābāhur asmatpriyahite rataḥ bhavāṃś ca puruṣavyāghra sarvalokamahārathaḥ tasmiñ jayāśā vipulā mama madrajanādhipa
english: Karṇa alone, the mighty-armed, is devoted to our welfare and delight, and you too, O tiger among men, are a great chariot-warrior of all the worlds; in him my hope of victory is vast, O lord of the Madra folk.

sanskrit: pārthasya samare kṛṣṇo yathābhīśuvaragrahaḥ tena yukto raṇe pārtho rakṣyamāṇaś ca pārthiva yāni karmāṇi kurute pratyakṣāṇi tathaiva te
english: As Kṛṣṇa is the supreme holder of the reins for Pārtha in battle, joined with whom and guarded by whom in the fight, O king, Pārtha performs the deeds that lie plain before your very eyes—

sanskrit: pūrvaṃ na samare hy evam avadhīd arjuno ripūn ahany ahani madreśa drāvayan dṛśyate yudhi
english: never before in battle did Arjuna slay enemies thus; yet day after day, O lord of the Madras, he is seen routing them in the fray.

sanskrit: bhāgo 'vaśiṣṭaḥ karṇasya tava caiva mahādyute taṃ bhāgaṃ saha karṇena yugapan nāśayāhave
english: There remains a share for Karṇa and for you, O greatly radiant one; that share, together with Karṇa, destroy at one stroke in the battle.

sanskrit: sūryāruṇau yathā dṛṣṭvā tamo naśyati māriṣa tathā naśyantu kaunteyāḥ sapāñcālāḥ sasṛñjayāḥ
english: As at the sight of the sun and his red dawn the darkness perishes, O honored one, so let the sons of Kuntī perish with the Pāñcālas and the Sṛñjayas.

sanskrit: rathānāṃ pravaraḥ karṇo yantṝṇāṃ pravaro bhavān saṃnipātaḥ samo loke bhavator nāsti kaś cana
english: Karṇa is the foremost of chariot-warriors, and you are the foremost of charioteers; in all the world there is no union of two equal to yours.

sanskrit: yathā sarvāsv avasthāsu vārṣṇeyaḥ pāti pāṇḍavam tathā bhavān paritrātu karṇaṃ vaikartanaṃ raṇe
english: As in every circumstance the Vārṣṇeya guards the Pāṇḍava, so let you wholly protect Karṇa Vaikartana in the battle.

sanskrit: tvayā sārathinā hy eṣa apradhṛṣyo bhaviṣyati devatānām api raṇe saśakrāṇāṃ mahīpate kiṃ punaḥ pāṇḍaveyānāṃ mātiśaṅkīr vaco mama
english: With you as his charioteer he will become unassailable in war even by the gods led by Śakra, O lord of earth—how much more so by the sons of Pāṇḍu! Do not doubt my word overmuch.

sanskrit: duryodhanavacaḥ śrutvā śalyaḥ krodhasamanvitaḥ triśikhāṃ bhrukuṭīṃ kṛtvā dhunvan hastau punaḥ punaḥ
english: Hearing Duryodhana's words, Śalya, filled with wrath, drew his brow into a triple-furrowed frown, shaking his hands again and again.

sanskrit: krodharakte mahānetre parivartya mahābhujaḥ kulaiśvaryaśrutibalair dṛptaḥ śalyo 'bravīd idam
english: Rolling his great eyes red with anger, the mighty-armed Śalya, proud in the strength of lineage, sovereignty, and sacred learning, spoke these words:

sanskrit: avamanyase māṃ gāndhāre dhruvaṃ māṃ pariśaṅkase yan māṃ bravīṣi visrabdhaṃ sārathyaṃ kriyatām iti
english: You hold me in contempt, son of Gāndhārī, and surely you mistrust me, in that you tell me so freely, 'Let the charioteering be done.'

sanskrit: asmatto 'bhyadhikaṃ karṇaṃ manyamānaḥ praśaṃsasi na cāhaṃ yudhi rādheyaṃ gaṇaye tulyam ātmanā
english: Deeming Karṇa greater than myself, you sing his praises; but I do not reckon Rādheya in battle as the equal of myself.

sanskrit: ādiśyatām abhyadhiko mamāṃśaḥ pṛthivīpate tam ahaṃ samare hatvā gamiṣyāmi yathāgatam
english: Let a greater share be assigned to me, O lord of earth; having slain that share in battle, I shall depart as I came.

sanskrit: atha vāpy eka evāhaṃ yotsyāmi kurunandana paśya vīryaṃ mamādya tvaṃ saṃgrāme dahato ripūn
english: Or else I shall fight, I alone, O delight of the Kurus; behold today my valor in battle as I consume the foe.

sanskrit: na cābhikāmān kauravya vidhāya hṛdaye pumān asmadvidhaḥ pravarteta mā mā tvam atiśaṅkithāḥ
english: A man of my kind, O Kaurava, would not act after harboring such designs in his heart; do not, do not doubt me overmuch.

sanskrit: yudhi cāpy avamāno me na kartavyaḥ kathaṃ cana paśya hīmau mama bhujau vajrasaṃhananopamau
english: And in battle no slight whatsoever should be offered me; behold these two arms of mine, firm-knit as the thunderbolt itself.

sanskrit: dhanuḥ paśya ca me citraṃ śarāṃś cāśīviṣopamān rathaṃ paśya ca me kḷptaṃ sadaśvair vātavegitaiḥ gadāṃ ca paśya gāndhāre hemapaṭṭavibhūṣitām
english: Behold my wondrous bow, and my arrows like venomous serpents; behold my chariot well-arrayed with noble steeds swift as the wind, and behold, son of Gāndhārī, my mace adorned with bands of gold.

sanskrit: dārayeyaṃ mahīṃ kruddho vikireyaṃ ca parvatān śoṣayeyaṃ samudrāṃś ca tejasā svena pārthiva
english: In wrath I could cleave the earth, scatter the mountains, and dry up the oceans by my own fiery might, O king.

sanskrit: tan mām evaṃvidhaṃ jānan samartham arinigrahe kasmād yunakṣi sārathye nyūnasyādhirather nṛpa
english: Knowing me, then, to be of such a kind and able to subdue the foe, why do you yoke me to the charioteering of one lesser, the son of a charioteer, O king?

sanskrit: na nāma dhuri rājendra prayoktuṃ tvam ihārhasi na hi pāpīyasaḥ śreyān bhūtvā preṣyatvam utsahe
english: Truly you ought not, O lord of kings, to harness me thus in service; for being the better, I cannot bear to do the bidding of a worse man.

sanskrit: yo hy abhyupagataṃ prītyā garīyāṃsaṃ vaśe sthitam vaśe pāpīyaso dhatte tat pāpam adharottaram
english: He who places under the sway of a lesser man one who is greater, who out of affection has come and submitted to his power—that is a sin that turns the higher to the lower.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇā brahmaṇā sṛṣṭā mukhāt kṣatram athorasaḥ ūrubhyām asṛjad vaiśyāñ śūdrān padbhyām iti śrutiḥ tebhyo varṇaviśeṣāś ca pratilomānulomajāḥ
english: The brāhmaṇas were created by Brahmā from his mouth, the kṣatra from his breast; from his thighs he brought forth the vaiśyas, and the śūdras from his feet—so says the śruti; and from these arise the distinct mixed castes, born against and along the grain of the orders.

sanskrit: athānyonyasya saṃyogāc cāturvarṇyasya bhārata goptāraḥ saṃgrahītāro dātāraḥ kṣatriyāḥ smṛtāḥ
english: And from the union of these four orders one with another, O Bhārata, the kṣatriyas are declared to be protectors, gatherers, and givers.

sanskrit: yājanādhyāpanair viprā viśuddhaiś ca pratigrahaiḥ lokasyānugrahārthāya sthāpitā brahmaṇā bhuvi
english: The brāhmaṇas, by officiating at sacrifices, by teaching, and by accepting pure gifts, were established by Brahmā upon the earth for the welfare of the world.

sanskrit: kṛṣiś ca pāśupālyaṃ ca viśāṃ dānaṃ ca sarvaśaḥ brahmakṣatraviśāṃ śūdrā vihitāḥ paricārakāḥ
english: Tillage, the herding of cattle, and giving in every form are the duties of the vaiśyas; and the śūdras are ordained as the servants of brāhmaṇa, kṣatriya, and vaiśya.

sanskrit: brahmakṣatrasya vihitāḥ sūtā vai paricārakāḥ na viṭśūdrasya tatraiva śṛṇu vākyaṃ mamānagha
english: The sūtas are ordained as servants of the brāhmaṇa and the kṣatriya, and not of the vaiśya or the śūdra; in this very matter hear my word, O sinless one.

sanskrit: so 'haṃ mūrdhāvasiktaḥ san rājarṣikulasaṃbhavaḥ mahārathaḥ samākhyātaḥ sevyaḥ stavyaś ca bandinām
english: I, being a consecrated king, sprung from a line of royal sages, am proclaimed a great chariot-warrior, one to be served and to be hymned by the bards.

sanskrit: so 'ham etādṛśo bhūtvā nehārikulamardana sūtaputrasya saṃgrāme sārathyaṃ kartum utsahe
english: Being such a one, O crusher of hostile clans, I cannot bring myself to do charioteering for the son of a charioteer in battle.

sanskrit: avamānam ahaṃ prāpya na yotsyāmi kathaṃ cana āpṛcchya tvādya gāndhāre gamiṣyāmi yathāgatam
english: Having met with this insult, I will not fight at all; taking my leave of you this day, son of Gāndhārī, I shall go as I came.

sanskrit: evam uktvā naravyāghraḥ śalyaḥ samitiśobhanaḥ utthāya prayayau tūrṇaṃ rājamadhyād amarṣitaḥ
english: Having spoken thus, Śalya, that tiger among men, the ornament of assemblies, rose and swiftly departed from the midst of the kings, full of indignation.

sanskrit: praṇayād bahumānāc ca taṃ nigṛhya sutas tava abravīn madhuraṃ vākyaṃ sāma sarvārthasādhakam
english: But your son, restraining him out of love and high regard, spoke sweet and conciliatory words that accomplish every purpose:

sanskrit: yathā śalya tvam ātthedam evam etad asaṃśayam abhiprāyas tu me kaś cit taṃ nibodha janeśvara
english: As you have said this, O Śalya, so it is without doubt; yet I have a certain intention—mark it, O lord of men.

sanskrit: na karṇo 'bhyadhikas tvattaḥ śaṅke naiva kathaṃ cana na hi madreśvaro rājā kuryād yad anṛtaṃ bhavet
english: Karṇa is not greater than you; I have no doubt of it in the least, nor would the king of the Madras do anything that would prove untrue.

sanskrit: ṛtam eva hi pūrvās te vahanti puruṣottamāḥ tasmād ārtāyaniḥ prokto bhavān iti matir mama
english: For your forefathers, those best of men, bore aloft the truth alone; and therefore you are called Ārtāyani—such is my conviction.

sanskrit: śalyabhūtaś ca śatrūṇāṃ yasmāt tvaṃ bhuvi mānada tasmāc chalyeti te nāma kathyate pṛthivīpate
english: And because on earth you are as a spear-point to your enemies, O bestower of honor, therefore your name is told as Śalya, O lord of earth.

sanskrit: yad eva vyāhṛtaṃ pūrvaṃ bhavatā bhūridakṣiṇa tad eva kuru dharmajña madarthaṃ yad yad ucyase
english: What you have already declared, O giver of abundant largesse—do that very thing, O knower of dharma, for my sake, whatever you are asked.

sanskrit: na ca tvatto hi rādheyo na cāham api vīryavān vṛṇīmas tvāṃ hayāgryāṇāṃ yantāram iti saṃyuge
english: Neither Rādheya nor I, valiant though we be, is greater than you; we choose you as the driver of his noble steeds in the encounter.

sanskrit: yathā hy abhyadhikaṃ karṇaṃ guṇais tāta dhanaṃjayāt vāsudevād api tvāṃ ca loko 'yam iti manyate
english: For just as this world holds Karṇa to surpass Dhanaṃjaya in qualities, so too it holds you, dear sir, to surpass even Vāsudeva.

sanskrit: karṇo hy abhyadhikaḥ pārthād astrair eva nararṣabha bhavān apy adhikaḥ kṛṣṇād aśvayāne bale tathā
english: Karṇa indeed surpasses Pārtha in weapons, O bull among men, and you too surpass Kṛṣṇa in the driving of horses and in strength alike.

sanskrit: yathāśvahṛdayaṃ veda vāsudevo mahāmanāḥ dviguṇaṃ tvaṃ tathā vettha madrarāja na saṃśayaḥ
english: As the great-minded Vāsudeva knows the very heart of horses, so do you know it twofold, O king of the Madras; there is no doubt of this.

sanskrit: śalya uvāca yan mā bravīṣi gāndhāre madhye sainyasya kaurava viśiṣṭaṃ devakīputrāt prītimān asmy ahaṃ tvayi
english: Śalya said: In that you call me, O son of Gāndhārī, in the midst of the host, O Kaurava, superior to the son of Devakī, I am well pleased with you.

sanskrit: eṣa sārathyam ātiṣṭhe rādheyasya yaśasvinaḥ yudhyataḥ pāṇḍavāgryeṇa yathā tvaṃ vīra manyase
english: So be it: I will undertake the charioteering of the renowned Rādheya as he fights with the foremost of the Pāṇḍavas, even as you wish, O hero.

sanskrit: samayaś ca hi me vīra kaś cid vaikartanaṃ prati utsṛjeyaṃ yathāśraddham ahaṃ vāco 'sya saṃnidhau
english: Yet I have one condition, O hero, with regard to Vaikartana: that I may utter freely in his presence whatever words I please.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tatheti rājan putras te saha karṇena bhārata abravīn madrarājasya sutaṃ bharatasattama
english: Saṃjaya said: 'So be it,' O king, said your son together with Karṇa, O Bhārata, to the son of the Madra king, O best of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: duryodhana uvāca bhūya eva tu madreśa yat te vakṣyāmi tac chṛṇu yathā purā vṛttam idaṃ yuddhe devāsure vibho
english: Duryodhana said: Yet further, O lord of the Madras, hear what I shall tell you—how this came to pass of old in the war between the gods and the asuras, O mighty one.

sanskrit: yad uktavān pitur mahyaṃ mārkaṇḍeyo mahān ṛṣiḥ tad aśeṣeṇa bruvato mama rājarṣisattama tvaṃ nibodha na cāpy atra kartavyā te vicāraṇā
english: What Mārkaṇḍeya, the great sage, told to my father and to me—as I relate it in full, O best of royal sages, do you mark it, and let there be no questioning of it in your mind.

sanskrit: devānām asurāṇāṃ ca mahān āsīt samāgamaḥ babhūva prathamo rājan saṃgrāmas tārakāmayaḥ nirjitāś ca tadā daityā daivatair iti naḥ śrutam
english: There was a great clash of the gods and the asuras, O king; the first battle, the one centered on Tāraka, took place, and then the daityas were vanquished by the gods—so we have heard.

sanskrit: nirjiteṣu ca daityeṣu tārakasya sutās trayaḥ tārākṣaḥ kamalākṣaś ca vidyunmālī ca pārthiva
english: And when the daityas had been vanquished, there were three sons of Tāraka—Tārākṣa, Kamalākṣa, and Vidyunmālin, O king.

sanskrit: tapa ugraṃ samāsthāya niyame parame sthitāḥ tapasā karśayām āsur dehān svāñ śatrutāpana
english: Undertaking fierce austerity and abiding in the highest self-restraint, they wasted their own bodies through penance, O tormentor of foes.

sanskrit: damena tapasā caiva niyamena ca pārthiva teṣāṃ pitāmahaḥ prīto varadaḥ pradadau varān
english: By their subjugation of the senses, their austerity, and their self-restraint, O king, the Grandsire, well pleased, the bestower of boons, granted them boons.

sanskrit: avadhyatvaṃ ca te rājan sarvabhūteṣu sarvadā sahitā varayām āsuḥ sarvalokapitāmaham
english: And together they begged of the Grandsire of all the worlds, O king, this boon: invulnerability among all beings for all time.

sanskrit: tān abravīt tadā devo lokānāṃ prabhur īśvaraḥ nāsti sarvāmaratvaṃ hi nivartadhvam ato 'surāḥ varam anyaṃ vṛṇīdhvaṃ vai yādṛśaṃ saṃprarocate
english: Then the god, the lord and master of the worlds, said to them: 'There is no such thing as complete immortality; turn back from this, O asuras, and choose some other boon, whatever pleases you well.'

sanskrit: tatas te sahitā rājan saṃpradhāryāsakṛd bahu sarvalokeśvaraṃ vākyaṃ praṇamyainam athābruvan
english: Then, O king, the three together, having deliberated again and again at length, bowed before the lord of all the worlds and spoke this word:

sanskrit: asmākaṃ tvaṃ varaṃ deva prayacchemaṃ pitāmaha vayaṃ purāṇi trīṇy eva samāsthāya mahīm imām vicariṣyāma loke 'smiṃs tvatprasādapuraskṛtāḥ
english: Grant us this boon, O god, O Grandsire: that we, dwelling in three cities, may roam over this earth and through this world, set forward by your grace.

sanskrit: tato varṣasahasre tu sameṣyāmaḥ parasparam ekībhāvaṃ gamiṣyanti purāṇy etāni cānagha
english: Then, after a thousand years, we shall come together one with another, and these cities shall pass into a single union, O sinless one.

sanskrit: samāgatāni caitāni yo hanyād bhagavaṃs tadā ekeṣuṇā devavaraḥ sa no mṛtyur bhaviṣyati evam astv iti tān devaḥ pratyuktvā prāviśad divam
english: And whoever then, O blessed one, should destroy these cities once they have come together, with a single arrow—that best of gods shall be our death.' 'So be it,' the god replied to them, and entered heaven.

sanskrit: te tu labdhavarāḥ prītāḥ saṃpradhārya parasparam puratrayavisṛṣṭyarthaṃ mayaṃ vavrur mahāsuram viśvakarmāṇam ajaraṃ daityadānavapūjitam
english: Having gained their boon and rejoicing, they took counsel together and, for the fashioning of the three cities, chose Maya, the great asura, the all-maker, the ageless one, honored by daityas and dānavas.

sanskrit: tato mayaḥ svatapasā cakre dhīmān purāṇi ha trīṇi kāñcanam ekaṃ tu raupyaṃ kārṣṇāyasaṃ tathā
english: Then the wise Maya, by his own austerity, made three cities: one of gold, one of silver, and one of black iron.

sanskrit: kāñcanaṃ divi tatrāsīd antarikṣe ca rājatam āyasaṃ cābhavad bhūmau cakrasthaṃ pṛthivīpate
english: The golden one stood there in heaven, the silver in mid-air, and the iron one upon the earth, set as upon a wheel, O lord of earth.

sanskrit: ekaikaṃ yojanaśataṃ vistārāyāmasaṃmitam gṛhāṭṭāṭṭālakayutaṃ bṛhatprākāratoraṇam
english: Each one measured a hundred yojanas in breadth and in length, furnished with houses and towers and lofty watch-platforms, and great ramparts and gateways.

sanskrit: guṇaprasavasaṃbādham asaṃbādham anāmayam prāsādair vividhaiś caiva dvāraiś cāpy upaśobhitam
english: Thronged with the increase of every excellence, yet uncrowded and free of all ill, each was adorned with palaces of many kinds and with portals as well.

sanskrit: pureṣu cābhavan rājan rājāno vai pṛthak pṛthak kāñcanaṃ tārakākṣasya citram āsīn mahātmanaḥ rājataṃ kamalākṣasya vidyunmālina āyasam
english: And in the cities there were kings, O king, each apart: the wondrous golden one belonged to great-souled Tārākṣa, the silver to Kamalākṣa, and the iron to Vidyunmālin.

sanskrit: trayas te daityarājānas trīṃl lokān āśu tejasā ākramya tasthur varṣāṇāṃ pūgān nāma prajāpatiḥ
english: Those three daitya-kings, overrunning the three worlds swiftly by their fiery might, stood firm for whole hosts of years, as a Prajāpati.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ dānavamukhyānāṃ prayutāny arbudāni ca koṭyaś cāprativīrāṇāṃ samājagmus tatas tataḥ mahad aiśvaryam icchantas tripuraṃ durgam āśritāḥ
english: Of those foremost dānavas there gathered from here and there millions and hundreds of millions, yea crores of warriors without rival, who, longing for great dominion, took refuge in the unassailable Tripura.

sanskrit: sarveṣāṃ ca punas teṣāṃ sarvayogavaho mayaḥ tam āśritya hi te sarve avartantākutobhayāḥ
english: And Maya, the provider of every need, was the support of them all; relying upon him, they all dwelt without fear from any quarter.

sanskrit: yo hi yaṃ manasā kāmaṃ dadhyau tripurasaṃśrayaḥ tasmai kāmaṃ mayas taṃ taṃ vidadhe māyayā tadā
english: Whatever desire any dweller of Tripura conceived in his mind, that very desire Maya then provided for him by his magic art.

sanskrit: tārakākṣasutaś cāsīd dharir nāma mahābalaḥ tapas tepe paramakaṃ yenātuṣyat pitāmahaḥ
english: And there was a son of Tārākṣa, Hari by name, of great strength, who performed the highest austerity, by which the Grandsire was well pleased.

sanskrit: sa tuṣṭam avṛṇod devaṃ vāpī bhavatu naḥ pure śastrair vinihatā yatra kṣiptāḥ syur balavattarāḥ
english: He begged of the well-pleased god: 'Let there be in our city a well into which the slain, struck down by weapons, may be cast and rise up mightier than before.'

sanskrit: sa tu labdhvā varaṃ vīras tārakākṣasuto hariḥ sasṛje tatra vāpīṃ tāṃ mṛtānāṃ jīvanīṃ prabho
english: And having gained the boon, the hero Hari, son of Tārākṣa, fashioned there that well, the giver of life to the dead, O lord.

sanskrit: yena rūpeṇa daityas tu yena veṣeṇa caiva ha mṛtas tasyāṃ parikṣiptas tādṛśenaiva jajñivān
english: In whatever form and in whatever guise a daitya had died, cast into that well he was reborn in that very same form.

sanskrit: tāṃ prāpya traipurasthās tu sarvāṃl lokān babādhire mahatā tapasā siddhāḥ surāṇāṃ bhayavardhanāḥ na teṣām abhavad rājan kṣayo yuddhe kathaṃ cana
english: Having won that well, the dwellers of Tripura oppressed all the worlds; perfected by great austerity and multipliers of the gods' terror, they suffered no loss whatever in battle, O king.

sanskrit: tatas te lobhamohābhyām abhibhūtā vicetasaḥ nirhrīkāḥ saṃsthitiṃ sarve sthāpitāṃ samalūlupan
english: Then, overcome by greed and delusion and bereft of sense, all of them, grown shameless, transgressed the established order that had been ordained.

sanskrit: vidrāvya sagaṇān devāṃs tatra tatra tadā tadā viceruḥ svena kāmena varadānena darpitāḥ
english: Routing the gods together with their hosts here and there, time and again, they roamed at their own pleasure, made arrogant by the granting of the boon.

sanskrit: devāraṇyāni sarvāṇi priyāṇi ca divaukasām ṛṣīṇām āśramān puṇyān yūpāñ janapadāṃs tathā vyanāśayanta maryādā dānavā duṣṭacāriṇaḥ
english: All the sacred groves of the gods and the haunts dear to the dwellers of heaven, the holy hermitages of the sages, the sacrificial posts, and the settled lands—these the dānavas, evil in their conduct, destroyed, transgressing every bound.

sanskrit: te devāḥ sahitāḥ sarve pitāmaham ariṃdama abhijagmus tadākhyātuṃ viprakāraṃ suretaraiḥ
english: All those gods together, O subduer of foes, went up to the Grandsire to tell of the outrage wrought by the foes of the gods.

sanskrit: te tattvaṃ sarvam ākhyāya śirasābhipraṇamya ca vadhopāyam apṛcchanta bhagavantaṃ pitāmaham
english: Having related the whole truth and bowed their heads in reverence, they asked the blessed Grandsire for a means to slay them.

sanskrit: śrutvā tad bhagavān devo devān idam uvāca ha asurāś ca durātmānas te cāpi vibudhadviṣaḥ aparādhyanti satataṃ ye yuṣmān pīḍayanty uta
english: Hearing that, the blessed god spoke this to the gods: 'Those evil-souled asuras, those haters of the wise, who continually offend against you and afflict you—'
